sourcedFrom: Aero Precision Gun Safety and Instruction Manual — Gun Safety and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) (cached from a 2021 capture)
cleanIntro: Aero's .308 AR — a larger receiver set than the 5.56 guns but the same direct-impingement action, and the same book covers it. ⛔ LUBRICATE BY WEIGHT: GENEROUS on the bolt, gas rings and the carrier's cam pin area; LIGHT on the firing pin, charging handle and the carrier's outer surfaces; the carrier key DRIED with a pipe cleaner and then ONE drop of oil. ⚠ On a .308 the bolt and carrier are heavier and the buffer spring is stiffer — take the buffer out under control, because it leaves the tube harder than a 5.56 one does. ⛔ And the handguard stays on.

steps.title: Selector to SAFE, magazine out, bolt back
steps.action: Muzzle safe, hands away from the trigger and the ejection port. Selector to SAFE, press the magazine catch and take the magazine out, then pull the charging handle to the rear and push in the lower part of the bolt catch to lock the bolt open.
steps.prose: If the last round was fired with the magazine in, the carrier is already held to the rear — but check rather than assume, because a carrier that ran forward on a fresh round looks identical from the buttstock end.
steps.quote: Pull the charging handle to rear and push in lower portion of bolt catch. If a round had been in the chamber it should have been ejected.
steps.cite: Aero Precision Gun Safety and Instruction Manual — Gun Safety and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — To Unload the Rifle, printed p.11

steps.title: Look into the chamber and the magazine well
steps.action: With the bolt held open, look into the chamber through the ejection port and into the magazine well. Aero's instruction is to unload immediately after use and before any cleaning.
steps.prose: Do this now rather than after the pins come out — an AR with the upper hinged open no longer presents the chamber the same way.
steps.quote: Always unload your firearm immediately after use and prior to cleaning and storage to minimize the risk of accidental discharge.
steps.cite: Aero Precision Gun Safety and Instruction Manual — Gun Safety and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — To Unload the Rifle, printed p.11

steps.title: Rear takedown pin, pushed from the LEFT
steps.action: Press the rear takedown pin in from the LEFT side of the lower receiver and pull it out on the right until it comes to a positive stop. It is captive and does not leave the receiver.
steps.prose: "Positive stop" is the feel to wait for — pulling harder past it does not free anything and does chew the detent.
steps.quote: Press the rear take down pin in from the left side of the lower receiver. Pull the pin out on the right side of the receiver until it comes to a positive stop.
steps.cite: Aero Precision Gun Safety and Instruction Manual — Gun Safety and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — Disassembling the firearm, printed pp.14-23
steps.warn: Make sure that the magazine is removed and the firearm is unloaded so it cannot be fired.

steps.title: Hinge it open — and split it if you want to
steps.action: Pivot the lower receiver down and away from the upper. If you want the two halves fully separate, press the front pivot pin from the left and pull it out on the right to its stop.
steps.prose: Splitting them is worth doing for a real clean: it gives you the buffer tube and the whole lower interior, and it stops the upper hanging off the lower while you are brushing at it.
steps.quote: Pivot the lower receiver down and away from the upper receiver.
steps.cite: Aero Precision Gun Safety and Instruction Manual — Gun Safety and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — Disassembling the firearm, printed pp.14-23

steps.title: Bolt carrier group, then the charging handle
steps.action: Pull the charging handle to the rear and draw the bolt carrier group out. Then take the charging handle back to its keyway and drop it down and out of the upper.
steps.prose: Carrier first, handle second — the handle cannot reach its keyway while the carrier is still riding on it.
steps.aside: Remove the charging handle Pg 21 by pulling it backwards to keyway and then down and out of the upper receiver.
steps.quote: Pull charging handle to the rear and remove the bolt carrier group.
steps.cite: Aero Precision Gun Safety and Instruction Manual — Gun Safety and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — Disassembling the firearm, printed pp.14-23

steps.title: Bore from the chamber, patches until clean
steps.action: Attach a cotton flannel patch to the rod, insert at the chamber and pass rod and patch down through the barrel. Change the patch every pass and repeat until one comes out clean.
steps.prose: Aero's materials list is specific: patches cut to fit SNUGLY, a brass wire bore brush, a chamber brush, gun solution and a light gun oil. A loose patch skates over fouling instead of taking it out.
steps.quote: Attach a cotton flannel patch to end of the cleaning rod, insert it into the chamber and pass the rod and patch down through the barrel. Repeat, changing patches with each pass through the barrel, until the patch comes out clean.
steps.cite: Aero Precision Gun Safety and Instruction Manual — Gun Safety and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — Cleaning and lubricating the firearm, printed pp.26-29

steps.title: Brass brush all the way through — never reverse
steps.action: If the bore is still dirty, dip the brass wire bore brush in solution and scrub, passing the brush ALL THE WAY through before reversing.
steps.prose: Aero gives the practical reason rather than the theoretical one: change direction with the brush in the barrel and the brush sticks. That is how bristles end up in a bore.
steps.quote: Thoroughly scrub out the barrel, passing the brush all the way through the barrel before reversing the movement. If you try to change direction with the brush in the barrel, the brush will stick.
steps.cite: Aero Precision Gun Safety and Instruction Manual — Gun Safety and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — Cleaning and lubricating the firearm, printed pp.26-29

steps.title: Chamber: five plunges and three full turns
steps.action: Fit the larger chamber brush, dip it in bore cleaning solution, and give the chamber a minimum of five plunge strokes and three full 360-degree clockwise rotations. Then patch the bore again.
steps.prose: The rotations are what reach the shoulder and the lug recesses. Numbers rather than "until clean" because you cannot see in there.
steps.quote: Dip the brush in the bore cleaning solution and clean the chamber. Use a minimum of five plunge strokes and three 360 clockwise, rotational strokes.
steps.cite: Aero Precision Gun Safety and Instruction Manual — Gun Safety and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — Cleaning and lubricating the firearm, printed pp.26-29

steps.title: ⛔ Gas tube, locking lugs, gas rings, extractor lip
steps.action: With the bore brush still wet with solution, clean all carbon and powder residue from around the gas tube in the upper receiver, the bolt locking lugs, the bolt rings, the firing pin, the cam pin, the lip of the extractor and the inside of the bolt carrier group.
steps.prose: ⛔ This is where a direct-impingement rifle actually gets dirty, and where it stops working when it is not cleaned. The extractor lip in particular collects a carbon ring that changes how the claw sits on a case rim.
steps.quote: Use bore cleaning brush, still wet with firearm cleaning solution, and clean all carbon and powder residue from around the gas tube in the upper receiver, bolt locking lugs, bolt rings, firing pin, bolt cam pin, lip of the extractor, and inside the bolt carrier group.
steps.cite: Aero Precision Gun Safety and Instruction Manual — Gun Safety and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — Cleaning and lubricating the firearm, printed pp.26-29

steps.title: ⛔ Lubricate light here, GENEROUS there
steps.action: Light: the inside of the upper, the bore and chamber, the outside of the barrel and the surfaces under the handguard; the firing pin and its recess; the charging handle, the carrier's inner and outer surfaces, the extractor and its pin — and the carrier key dried with a pipe cleaner then ONE drop of oil. GENEROUS: the slide and cam pin area of the carrier, the bolt, the gas rings, and every moving part in the lower with its pins and detents.
steps.prose: ⛔ Aero splits it exactly this way for a reason. The bolt and the cam pin area take the heat and the rubbing; the firing pin channel and the carrier key do not, and oil there only collects carbon.
steps.aside: Be sure you lube in and around all the locking lugs. Depress the front sight detent and apply 2-3 drops of oil. Depress the detent several times to work the lubricant into the spring.
steps.quote: The inside of the carrier key should be dried with a pipe cleaner, then place one drop of oil inside.
steps.cite: Aero Precision Gun Safety and Instruction Manual — Gun Safety and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — Cleaning and lubricating the firearm, printed pp.26-29

steps.title: ⛔ Check for bristles, then take the fingerprints off
steps.action: Before anything goes back together, check that no flannel or brush bristles have lodged anywhere. Then wipe cleaning solution, oil and fingerprints off every outside surface.
steps.prose: ⛔ Aero puts the bristle check as its own numbered step ahead of lubrication, and it is the right place for it. Fingerprints matter too: finger moisture left on steel starts corrosion.
steps.aside: Remove any gun cleaning solution, oil and finger prints from the outside surfaces of the firearm. Finger moisture, if left, could start a corrosion process.
steps.quote: Check that flannel or brush bristles have not become lodged in any part of the firearm, then lightly lubricate the following parts.
steps.cite: Aero Precision Gun Safety and Instruction Manual — Gun Safety and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — Cleaning and lubricating the firearm, printed pp.26-29

steps.title: Handguard: air, not removal
steps.action: If dirt has collected in or around the handguard, blow it out with compressed air and lubricate as needed. Do not take the handguard off to clean it.
steps.prose: ⛔ Aero is explicit that removal is not necessary unless dirt has actually accumulated in there — and that if it does need to come off, the rifle goes to a gunsmith. A free-float tube is torqued to a spec.
steps.aside: If removal of handguard is deemed necessary, please take rifle to a qualified gunsmith.
steps.quote: Removal is not necessary unless dirt has accumulated in or around the handguard.
steps.cite: Aero Precision Gun Safety and Instruction Manual — Gun Safety and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — Handguard Maintenance, printed p.24

steps.title: Field strip complete — four groups
steps.action: Upper receiver, lower receiver, bolt carrier group and charging handle. Deeper than this is the carrier group itself, which Aero does publish — it is the DEEP CLEAN below.
steps.prose: ⛔ And past THAT, Aero is explicit: do not strip the firearm further than it describes.
steps.quote: Do not strip your firearm further than previously described. If additional maintenance is required, see the "Service and Repair" section.
steps.cite: Aero Precision Gun Safety and Instruction Manual — Gun Safety and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — Disassembling the firearm, printed pp.14-23

deepSteps.title: Firing pin retaining pin, right to left
deepSteps.action: Push the firing pin retaining pin in from the RIGHT side of the bolt carrier group and pull it out on the left.
deepSteps.prose: Directional, and it matters — the pin is stepped and driving it the wrong way is how it deforms.
deepSteps.quote: Push in the firing pin retaining pin right to left of the bolt carrier group and remove it by pulling it out to the left.
deepSteps.cite: Aero Precision Gun Safety and Instruction Manual — Gun Safety and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — Disassembling the firearm, printed pp.14-23

deepSteps.title: Tilt the bolt face UP, and let the firing pin out
deepSteps.action: Turn the carrier so the bolt face points up, and take the firing pin out of the rear of the carrier.
deepSteps.prose: Bolt face up means the pin slides out under gravity rather than needing to be shaken free — and a shaken firing pin lands on its tip.
deepSteps.quote: Tilt the bolt face up and remove the firing pin.
deepSteps.cite: Aero Precision Gun Safety and Instruction Manual — Gun Safety and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — Disassembling the firearm, printed pp.14-23

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Push the bolt IN, then turn the cam pin 90 degrees
deepSteps.action: Push the bolt in toward the carrier until it rotates and stops, then turn the bolt cam pin 90 degrees and lift it out away from the carrier.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ Bolt in first. The cam pin sits under the gas key and cannot come out until the bolt is pushed back — trying to lift it with the bolt extended is what bends cam pins.
deepSteps.aside: Remove the cam pin by lifting it out away from the bolt carrier.
deepSteps.quote: Push the bolt in towards the carrier until the bolt rotates and comes to a stop, then turn the bolt cam pin 90.
deepSteps.cite: Aero Precision Gun Safety and Instruction Manual — Gun Safety and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — Disassembling the firearm, printed pp.14-23

deepSteps.title: Bolt forward out of the carrier
deepSteps.action: Pull the bolt forward and out of the carrier. Clean the carbon off the bolt tail, out of the carrier bore and off the three gas rings.
deepSteps.prose: The bolt tail is the dirtiest single surface on a DI rifle and the one most often left. A brass scraper or a fingernail-and-solvent is enough; do not go at it with anything that removes metal.
deepSteps.quote: Pull the bolt forward and remove it from the bolt carrier.
deepSteps.cite: Aero Precision Gun Safety and Instruction Manual — Gun Safety and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — Disassembling the firearm, printed pp.14-23

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Buffer and action spring — under tension
deepSteps.action: With the lower separate, depress the buffer and KEEP the pressure on, then depress the buffer retainer pin. Ease the buffer and spring forward out of the receiver extension, depressing the hammer to let them clear.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ The buffer is spring-loaded and Aero warns that it will be ejected if the retainer is released without holding it. It comes out at face height on a rifle held normally.
deepSteps.quote: Depress the buffer and maintain pressure, as the buffer is under spring tension, to prevent it from being ejected when the buffer retainer pin is depressed.
deepSteps.cite: Aero Precision Gun Safety and Instruction Manual — Gun Safety and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — Disassembling the firearm, printed pp.14-23

deepSteps.title: Clean the buffer tube, then back together — cam pin FIRST
deepSteps.action: Wipe the buffer, the action spring and the inside of the receiver extension. Then rebuild: buffer and spring back in with the retainer holding them, bolt into the carrier with the chamfered edge under the cam pin facing DOWN, cam pin in, rotate 90 degrees, firing pin, retaining pin left to right.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ Aero gives a second way to check the bolt is the right way round: the extractor should be oriented to the RIGHT side of the carrier. Use both checks — a bolt in backwards will assemble and will not extract.
deepSteps.quote: Another way to ensure proper bolt installation is to ensure that the extractor is oriented to the right side of the bolt carrier.
deepSteps.cite: Aero Precision Gun Safety and Instruction Manual — Gun Safety and Instruction Manual (no form code printed) — Reassembling the firearm, printed p.30
deepSteps.warn: If you attempt to fire without the bolt cam pin installed, damage or injury may result.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Snug-fitting flannel patches from the chamber, until one comes out clean
Brass brush ALL the way through before reversing
Chamber brush: 5 plunge strokes, 3 full clockwise turns

cleaning.name: BOLT CARRIER GROUP
tasks: Locking lugs, gas rings, extractor lip, inside the carrier
⛔ Carrier key DRIED with a pipe cleaner, then ONE drop of oil
Generous oil on the bolt, cam pin area and carrier slide rails

cleaning.name: UPPER RECEIVER
tasks: Carbon from around the gas tube
Light oil inside, on the bore, chamber and under the handguard
Front sight detent: 2-3 drops, worked in by depressing it

cleaning.name: LOWER RECEIVER
tasks: Buffer, action spring and inside the receiver extension
Generous oil on ALL moving lower parts, pins and detents
⛔ Check for lodged brush bristles before it goes back together

reassembly: Buffer and action spring into the receiver extension, retainer pin holding them.
Bolt into the carrier with the chamfered edge under the cam pin facing DOWN and the extractor to the RIGHT side of the carrier.
Cam pin in and rotated 90 degrees, then the firing pin, then the firing pin retaining pin from left to right.
Charging handle into the upper — forward about an inch into the keyway, then up.
Carrier in behind it, both forward into battery; then close the receivers and seat both pins.
Safety function check before the rifle goes away.
fncheck: Magazine out, chamber checked, muzzle safe. Pull the charging handle to the rear and let the bolt close — DO NOT pull the trigger; leave the hammer cocked. Selector to SAFE and pull the trigger: the hammer must not fall. Selector to FIRE and pull: it should fall. Then hold the trigger back, cycle the charging handle, and release the trigger SLOWLY — a quarter to a half of normal speed, no stops. You should hear a click and the hammer must NOT fall. ⛔ Repeat the FIRE test five times; if the rifle malfunctions in any of them it goes to a gunsmith.
